concepts.content: When the domestic interest rate exceeds the international interest rate, the current exchange rate must be above the expected future exchange rate so that the expected depreciation of the domestic currency offsets the higher domestic interest rate; conversely, if the domestic interest rate is lower, the current exchange rate is very depreciated because the currency is expected to appreciate to compensate for the interest rate differential.

source_grounding.validation_scope: exact quotation, chunk membership and field coverage only

evidence.quote:
If the domestic interest rate is above that,
 the international interest rate, then the exchange rate today
 has to be above the expected exchange rate,
 because that will give you a expected depreciation
 of the currency, which will compensate for the fact
 that the domestic bond is paying a higher interest
 rate than international bond.

Conversely, if the domestic bond is paying a lower interest
 rate, then the exchange rate today is very depreciated,
 because you have to expect it to appreciate in order
 to compensate for the interest rate differential.
